readyme.title: ReadyMe
readyme.subtitle: Redesigning a learning app end to end
readyme.lead: ReadyMe helps Sri Lankan students prepare for their G.C.E. A/L exams through structured learning paths built by tutors. I led a complete redesign of the live app, from the information architecture and flows to every screen and a new design system, turning a dense, subject-first app into a calm, discovery-led learning experience.
challenge: The original app worked, but it was built around a list of exam subjects. Students landed on a wall of similar cards, with a large subscribe banner competing for attention and no sense of what to study next.

Screens were dense: stats tiles, long topic tables, boxed answer options and several competing primary actions. Each flow looked slightly different, which made the product feel heavier than it needed to.
goals: Help students find the right learning path, tutor and content, instead of starting from a list of subjects.
Clear hierarchy, more whitespace and one obvious primary action per screen.
A design system of tokens and reusable components so every flow feels like the same product.

pairs.title: Home

Rich path cards with tutor, rating, language and subject tags

pairs.title: Course page

Four clear destinations: Learning materials, Analytics, Chat with tutor and Leaderboard

pairs.title: Answering questions

Image-led questions get room to breathe, with Quick ref one tap away
Answers move to their own view, toggled from a single bottom control

One clear primary action, Submit, instead of a dark Next bar
Previous / next and Question toggle stay in the same place on every question

pairs.title: Login

Google, Facebook and Apple sign-in as a compact row instead of full-width buttons
Clear “Create an account” path at the bottom

The plan choice is the only decision on the screen

glance: The app was organised around a fixed list of exam subjects. Students landed on near-identical cards, a permanent subscribe banner and no clear next step.
I audited every flow, rebuilt the navigation around learning, and designed a component system so every screen shares the same patterns and hierarchy.
A discovery-first home, a clear course hub, a calmer question flow and one consistent visual language across iOS, iPad and web.

audit: Home opened on a fixed list of exam subjects, so there was nothing to discover and no sense of what to do next.
Exam name, provider and plan were squeezed into small all-caps lines that were hard to scan.
Every subject card repeated the same two counters, so nothing stood out or invited a tap.
A floating action button sat on top of the list and covered part of a card.
A subscribe banner was pinned to the home screen before students had experienced any content.
One of three main tabs went to Settings, while finding and continuing learning had no clear home.
principles: Lead with content students want, and ask for a subscription only once they've seen its value.
Clear hierarchy, generous whitespace and a single obvious primary action on every screen.
Tokens and reusable components, so every flow feels like the same product and ships faster.

authoring.title: ReadyMe Authoring Tool
authoring.subtitle: Designing where tutors build learning
authoring.lead: Every learning path, question set, note, video and study deck in ReadyMe starts here. I designed the authoring tool end to end: the tutor's journey from sign-up and verification to creating, reviewing and publishing content, and getting paid.
stats: desktop screens designed across the tutor journey
flows and states, from onboarding to payouts
ways to add questions: type, PDF or image
challenge: Tutors are experts in their subject, not in software. To teach on ReadyMe they need to turn existing material such as papers, notes, videos and slides into structured, exam-ready content that students can trust.
The tool had to make that fast and calm, from verifying who they are and building a credible profile to creating content in several formats, checking it before students see it, and getting paid.
phases: Mapped the tutor's end-to-end job, from first sign-up to first payout, and every content type ReadyMe supports.
Turned that into principles, an information architecture and the core flows to design first.
Explored flows and layouts for creation, review and verification, including variants for key screens.
High-fidelity UI for every flow and state on desktop, with responsive layouts for smaller screens.
Reviewed flows with the team, iterated on V1/V2 versions of key screens and refined edge cases.
Handed off a component-based system with every state documented for engineering.

goals: Publish a complete learning path quickly
Reuse existing material instead of retyping it
Look credible so students choose their content
Get paid reliably for their work
pains: Typing hundreds of exam questions by hand
Not knowing what students will actually see

principles: Home is a teaching workspace, not a wall of reports. Creating is always one click away.
Long tasks are split into guided steps with validation as you go and a review before anything goes live.
Tutors can type questions, or extract them from a PDF or an image.
Identity, qualifications and experience build a public profile, with status always visible.

decisions.title: A teaching hub, not a dashboard
decisions.text: Home opens on “Your teaching resources”: question sets, notes, videos and study decks in one place, with a labelled side menu for paths, subscribers, notifications and settings.

decisions.title: Guided creation with a review step
decisions.text: Learning paths and question sets are built step by step, Set the details, then topics, then content, and always end in a review before publishing, with clear delete and publish confirmations.

decisions.title: Questions from PDFs and images
decisions.text: Instead of typing every question, tutors upload a PDF, run text extraction and turn it into a question set, or start from an image, with upload progress and file-type choices along the way.

decisions.title: Insight where it helps
decisions.text: A topic-distribution overview shows how a set's questions spread across topics, so gaps are visible before students find them.

decisions.title: Trust and payouts built in
decisions.text: Qualifications, professional experience and identity verification (NIC, driving licence or passport) feed a public tutor profile. Pending, approved and rejected states are designed for each step, and bank details unlock earnings.

decisions.title: A familiar welcome
decisions.text: Sign-in uses the same warm language and patterns as the student app, so tutors and students meet one ReadyMe brand.

metrics: How long a new tutor takes to publish their first learning path.
Share of learning paths and question sets that reach Review and get published.
